summary: API gateway 5xx wave caused by downstream fanout slowdown and runtime backlog
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC, FinQuick reported a sustained elevation of 5xx responses (502/503) from the Redwood API for their dedicated tenant. Impact: multiple customers endpoints experienced request failures and streaming session drops; customer reported lowered throughput and user-facing errors in prod. Environment: Dedicated capacity pool in us-east-1 serving mixed chat + large multipart embedding workloads. Observed behavior: API gateway returned 502/503s at ~8-12% error rate for 30+ minutes; apigw logs show upstream timeouts and connection resets. Serving runtime pods behind the route showed a backlog spike and several pods entering CrashLoopBackOff after NVML driver resets. Expected behavior: < 0.1% 5xx and graceful fallback to lower-capacity variants when runtime overloaded.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer replayed a high-throughput embedding upload (multipart, ~150 files, 2-4MB each) against their dedicated route
2) Simultaneously sent 200 small chat requests per second (concurrent sessions) to the same tenant route
3) Observe apigw error rate and runtime pod queues within 5 minutes of ramp
logs: apigw: 2026-03-10T09:18:03Z upstream timeout after 12s to 10.2.3.45:502 -> 502 returned to client
runtime-pod/k8s: 2026-03-10T09:19:11Z [nvml] GPU driver reset detected (reason: GPU page fault), pid=24321, container=runtime-v2
runtime: WARN prefetched-kv-lock held for 14.2s tenant=finquick shard=17
investigation_notes: 09:25 UTC - Support triage: Confirmed elevated 5xx on FinQuick tenant only; other tenants on same pool show mild elevation but significantly lower spread
09:35 UTC - SRE: Checked apigw accept queue depth and worker thread utilization; accept queue saturated during peak; worker threads spent time waiting on upstream connections
09:40 UTC - Observed correlation: NVML GPU resets on 3/12 runtime pods coincident with backlog spike. NVML logs indicate sporadic page faults and recoveries rather than immediate OOMs

09:55 UTC - Hypothesis A: large multipart embedding upload created heavy disk I/O and NVMe latency on ephemeral storage, slowing runtime cold loads -> longer model kernel selection -> upstream timeouts backpressure apigw
10:05 UTC - Hypothesis B: mixed small chat and large embedding workloads produced KV cache thrash and prefetch-lock contention causing runtime thread stalls and failed keepalives to apigw
10:20 UTC - Experiment: Scoped the tenant route to a lower concurrency in the dedicated pool via temporary rate-limit policy; error rate fell from ~10% to ~1.2% within 7 minutes
10:40 UTC - Note: One runtime pod showed repeated 'kernel fallback' traces which increase CPU path usage and raise latency for subsequent requests
11:05 UTC - Eng flagged a potential regression in prefetch cancellation logic (recent hotpatch 2026-03-08) as contributing factor; created INT-3309 for PR review
comments: FinQuick (support contact): 'We're seeing mid-morning failures across multiple users — some requests return 502 instantly, others hang then time out.' (2026-03-10 09:22 UTC)
Support (Aisha): 'Gathered logs and asked for request IDs. Initial mitigation: applied tenant-level soft rate-limit to reduce fanout. Monitoring now.' (2026-03-10 09:30 UTC)

SRE (Marco): 'I pushed a temporary routing policy that pins FinQuick to a smaller set of warm runtimes and limited concurrent embedding workers. Error rate decreased; continuing to monitor.' (2026-03-10 10:10 UTC)

Eng (Priya Menon): 'Investigating recent prefetch/cancellation hotpatchs. Reproduced a local workload that causes prefetch lock growth; preparing a revert PR if confirmed. See PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4189' (2026-03-10 11:00 UTC)
FinQuick: 'Thanks — we saw immediate improvement after rate-limit was applied. Please advise on root cause and long-term fix.' (2026-03-10 11:12 UTC)
Support: 'Raising to P1 and engaging Dedicated runtime on-call. We'll follow up with post-incident notes.' (2026-03-10 11:25 UTC)
SRE: 'Linking similar historical events: SUP-314159 (nightly-batch scheduler backpressure) showed identical accept-queue growth pattern; may be useful for runbook tweaks.' (2026-03-10 12:00 UTC)
resolution: Mitigation: Applied tenant-level soft rate limits and temporarily pinned FinQuick traffic to a smaller warm runtime subset; rolled back recent prefetch-cancellation hotpatch (hotfix PR github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4194) in the dedicated pool. Post-fix monitoring shows 5xx reduced to <0.2% and latency back within SLOs. Follow-ups: (1) Eng to add guardrails to prefetch cancellation to avoid lock growth (owner: Priya), (2) SRE to expand accept-queue autoscaling thresholds for dedicated pools during mixed-embedding workloads, (3) Runbook update to include temporary pinning steps for tenant-level blast radius reduction. Customer communicated resolution and asked for timeline on permanent fix.
